In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DFO induces neuronal cell death in vitro, and that surviving neurons are characterized by the up-regulation of HIF-1alpha and the down-regulation of hMOR mRNA expression.
DFO-induced hypoxic stress down-regulates the hMOR gene in a time- and dose-dependent manner at the transcriptional level.

DFO-induced hypoxic conditions down-regulate hMOR gene activity by a transcriptional mechanism, and that the down-regulation is mediated through both dsDNA and RNA elements located in a region of the hMOR gene promoter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DFO-induced hypoxic stress down-regulates the hMOR gene by a HIF-1alpha-independent mechanism.
DFO-induced hypoxic conditions down-regulate the hMOR mRNA level via a HIF-1alpha-dependent pathway, but do not alter hMOR mRNA turnover.

hypoxia, a condition that occurs under various pathophysiological conditions such as ischemic stroke or neurodegenerative diseases, may alter the expression of the hMOR gene, which could be a factor in the regulation of the opioid system in the CNS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hypoxemia induced by DFO is not a good model for the effects of opioid-induced respiratory depression.
hypoxia can down-regulate neuronal hMOR transcription by a mechanism that involves the HIF-1alpha and the hMOR promoter.
hypoxia can alter opioid receptor gene transcription, which may have important implications for the regulation of opioid receptor expression in the CNS during hypoxic/ischemic insults.
